newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt on shaky ground as election looms - poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt on shaky ground as election looms - poll.

text.p: A week before New Zealand's general election the main opposition Labour Party has dramatically closed the gap on the ruling conservative National Party, according to an opinion poll published on Saturday.
The poll in the Auckland-based New Zealand Herald showed Labour had jumped almost six points to 27.7 percent in a week, while National had dropped 2.8 points to 34 percent.

In the run-up to New Zealand's first election under proportional representation on October 12, the poll clearly showed that if the three main opposition parties were able to stitch together a coalition, they could form a government.

The New Zealand First Party was down four at 14 percent and the left-wing Alliance was up 0.6 points at 12.6 percent. The poll would give a Labour-New Zealand First-Alliance arrangement 73 seats in the 120 seat single chamber parliament.
It would also bring a Labour-New Zealand First or Labour- Alliance deal within striking distance of the 60 seats needed to command a majority.
National's likely coalition partners remained below the crucial five percent threshold at which parties who fail to win a constituency seat qualify for proportional representation in parliament.
Free-market ACT New Zealand was up 0.5 percent to 4.6 percent while the morals-based Christian Coalition was down marginally at four percent from 4.3 percent previously.
The poll was taken during a week which saw Labour leader Helen Clark emerge as the clear winner of the first televised political leaders debate.
